text: Proposition forty-two restricts certain future taxes.
The measure would prohibit new state taxes on
ownership of financial assets and other personal property.
It also limits certain retroactive taxes:
taxes applied to activities or periods before the
tax was adopted.
Prop forty-two could also prevent Prop forty’s wealth
tax from taking effect if both pass and
forty-two gets more yes votes.
A voter might favor predictable rules for savings,
investments, and business assets, or object to taxes
that reach backward.
Another voter could prefer deciding future tax proposals
individually instead of restricting them in the
constitution.
Yes imposes the new limits;
no retains the state’s current options without itself
creating a new tax.
